sentences.text: Serratia marcescens is an enteric bacterium that can act as an opportunistic pathogen, with increasing incidence reported in clinical settings.

This is attributed to a broad repertoire of virulence factors and acquired antibiotic resistance, and the World Health Organization has designated the species a research priority for alternative antimicrobial strategies.
Phylogenomic analysis in one study found the type II secretion system conserved among clinical isolates but absent from most environmental strains.

A retrospective review of a neonatal intensive care unit outbreak in Pretoria, South Africa reported 273 neonates with Serratia marcescens admitted between January 2022 and December 2023, with mortality 16.12%.
A case report describes the species as a rare colonizer of breast milk in the community setting, in a woman whose colonization resolved spontaneously while breastfeeding continued.
